4.text: To transfer an incantation is, however, no easy matter. Incantations are

5.text: given by supernatural protectors to a special person only, because the protector

6.text: had compassion for that person’s particular trouble. Therefore the incantations

7.text: are intended for the personal use of the one to whom given, and the super-

8.text: natural powers will be angry on the application of them to the use of another

9.text: person. Hence, even though a person is perfectly willing to transfer an

10.text: incantation, it may take several days of urging and persuasion before this

11.text: person will agree to proceed to the transmission. Through this method the

12.text: supernatural powers may see how serious is the need of the applicant, and

13.text: take compassion upon him also, which, of course, would assure the special

14.text: effectiveness of the incantation. Thus, in the case of incantations protecting

15.text: the life of small children, even the nearest relative, when he lives at a

16.text: distance, will repeatedly refuse to come to the house in need, and will consent

17.text: only after several attempts on the part of the parents of the child.

18.text: A shaman, however, is less scrupulous about giving his help. He asks

19.text: his “spirits” for a new incantation on behalf of the person applying, which,

20.text: in most cases, consists, not in words, but only in special prescribed actions.

21.text: On the contrary, he will try to keep for himself the “genuine incantations,”

22.text: the fruit of his knowledge, and will not transfer any of them without a special

24.text: The transference of incantations must not be made without pay of real

25.text: or at least of symbolical character, or the supernatural powers will be angry

26.text: with both parties, and the incantation will lose its force. Moreover, the

27.text: receiving party will be unable to keep in mind the words of the formula.

28.text: The transfer must be made without witnesses; otherwise, the incantation will

29.text: lose its power, or the third person, although unwillingly, will become pos-

31.text: The shaman, or any other person who wishes to practise the incantation

32.text: for his own use or in behalf of others, pronounces the formula in an inaudible

33.text: whisper; for, should even a stone hear the mysterious words, it would deprive

34.text: the owner of their possession, and gain them for itself. After finishing the

35.text: incantation, the person practising must spit at his left side, which is supposed

36.text: to fasten the incantation to the object in view. The same thing is done

37.text: when transferring the incantation to another person. The spitting indicates

38.text: that the possessor renounces the incantation, and gives it over to the other

39.text: party. According to a similar idea in a Koryak tale, Big-Raven sells his

40.text: daughter to a seal for a song, which the last-named spits into the mouth of

41.text: Big-Raven.¹ The incantations in dialogues, however, are pronounced aloud,
